officialSummary: Data on lending and deposit rates of scheduled commercial banks (SCBs) (excluding regional rural banks and small finance banks) received during October 2026 are set out in Tables 1 to 9. Highlights: Lending Rates: The weighted average lending rate (WALR) on outstanding rupee loans of SCBs remained unchanged at 8.96 per cent in September 2026 compared to August 2026. The WALR on fresh rupee loans of SCBs declined to 8.51 per cent in September 2026 from 8.61 per cent in August 2026. 1-Year median Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) of SCBs declined to 8.55 per cent in October 2026 from 8.61 per cent in September 2026. The WALR on fresh as well as outstanding rupee loans exhibited a mixed movement across sectors in September 2026. Deposit Rates: The weighted average domestic term deposit rate (WADTDR) on outstanding rupee term deposits of SCBs marginally declined to 6.55 per cent in September 2026 from 6.56 per cent in August 2026. The WADTDR on fresh rupee term deposits of SCBs declined to 5.61 per cent in September 2026 from 5.67 per cent in August 2026. Ajit Prasad Deputy General Manager (Communications) Press Release: 2026-2027/1416
title: Lending and Deposit Rates of Scheduled Commercial Banks – October 2026

officialSummary: The 625 th meeting of the Central Board of Directors of Reserve Bank of India was held today in Mumbai under the Chairmanship of Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor. The Central Board took the Integrity Pledge as part of the observance of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026. The Board in its meeting deliberated on the prevailing economic conditions and associated challenges and evaluated the potential risks to the economic outlook. The Board reviewed the activities of Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation and activities of select Central Office Departments of the Bank. Deputy Governors, Shri Swaminathan J., Dr. Poonam Gupta, Shri Shirish Chandra Murmu, Shri Rohit Jain, and other Directors of the Central Board, viz., Ms. Anuradha Thakur, Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs; Shri Anand Gopal Mahindra, Shri Janmejaya Kumar Sinha, Shri Syed Akbaruddin and Ms. Annie George Mathew attended the meeting. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1414

officialSummary: Data on sectoral deployment of bank credit for the month of September 2026, collected from 41 select scheduled commercial banks (SCBs), which together account for about 95 per cent of the total non-food credit by all SCBs 1 , are set out in Statements I and II . On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, non-food bank credit 2 grew by 19.1 per cent as on the fortnight ended September 30, 2026, compared to 11.2 per cent during the corresponding fortnight of the previous year (i.e., October 03, 2025). Highlights of the sectoral deployment of bank credit as on the fortnight ended September 30, 2026, are given below: Credit to agriculture and allied activities registered a y-o-y growth of 19.5 per cent vis-a-vis 8.9 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of the previous year. Credit to industry recorded a y-o-y growth of 19.5 per cent (7.7 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of last year). While credit to ‘large’ and ‘medium’ industries grew at an accelerated pace, ‘micro and small’ industries exhibited steady growth. Among major industries, credit to ‘infrastructure’, ‘basic metal and metal products’, ‘all engineering’, ‘chemical and chemical products’, ‘food processing’ and ‘textiles’ marked buoyant y-o-y growth. Credit to services sector registered a y-o-y growth of 28.3 per cent (9.9 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of the previous year), supported by buoyant growth in segments such as ‘non-banking financial companies’ (NBFCs), ‘trade’ ‘commercial real estate’, ‘transport operators’ and ‘professional services’. Credit to personal loans segment recorded a y-o-y growth of 17.3 per cent, as compared with 11.5 per cent a year ago. While credit growth in segments such as ‘housing’ and ‘vehicle loans’ remained resilient, ‘advances against fixed deposits’ accelerated. Growth in ‘loans against gold jewellery’ and ‘education’ decelerated compared to last year, albeit it remained strong. Ajit Prasad Deputy General Manager (Communications) Press Release: 2026-2027/1412 1 Dat
title: Sectoral Deployment of Bank Credit – September 2026
